plan.raw_excerpt:
External plan review (mode=iterate, provider=openrouter) — round 2 of 2.
Reviewers: openai = success (verdict: revise); gemini = degraded (reply cut off,
finish_reason=length) — recorded degraded, NOT counted as an approval.

Round 1 verdict: revise (6 findings). Round 2 verdict: revise (7 findings), with
the direction affirmed verbatim: "the enforcement direction and ordering are
sound, and the plan correctly preserves the intentional non-git SKIP and
cross-layer scope."

ROUND 2 FINDINGS (openai)

1. dependency / medium — Promoting layer_coverage._git_context into
   git_helpers.git_context() is sound reuse, but the plan does not specify the
   helper's contract or import constraints: it must not introduce a
   git_helpers -> layer_coverage cycle, change working-directory semantics, or
   leave existing tests patching the old symbol. Grep for patches/imports of
   _git_context, _git_precheck and _run_git; add focused tests for the shared
   helper itself.

2. edge-case / high — The plan does not say how git_context() reliably
   distinguishes not_git from git_error. A simple rev-parse non-zero is
   insufficient and stderr-text classification is brittle across git
   versions/locales. Timeouts and subprocess exceptions must be captured by the
   helper rather than escaping as an unstructured verifier exception. Preserve
   the existing decision logic exactly when extracting; reserve not_git for the
   verified outside-a-work-tree condition. Add exception/timeout tests.

3. edge-case / medium — "Missing or malformed iterate entry" is addressed at the
   return-value level, but the plan does not establish whether
   find_entry_by_run_id can itself raise while parsing malformed entry data. A
   precise boundary is needed between a corrupt results artifact (retains its
   distinct ERROR) and a valid artifact containing an absent/malformed entry
   (still produces the coverage finding). Normalize with isinstance(entry, dict);
   test both, asserting different details and that neither becomes a SKIP.

4. risk / medium — The replacement test set does not explicitly preserve
   successful behavior after the reorder. Retain/add: matching path + valid
   integration behavior passes; non-matching path passes even when no iterate
   entry exists; corrupt-results remains an ERROR only once the gate is
   applicable. Assert severity in each case.

5. edge-case / medium — Commit handling covers absent --commit and unresolvable
   HEAD, but not an invalid explicitly-supplied commit/base ref. That is a
   realistic CI invocation error and must reach the same fail-closed None/ERROR
   path rather than being treated as an empty diff. Verify the subprocess is
   invoked with argument arrays rather than shell interpolation.

6. approach / low — Updating the cross_component taxonomy prose while retaining
   min_complexity: "medium" is necessary but potentially confusing: that field
   still affects classification while the F11 gate now applies at every recorded
   complexity after diff applicability is found. State directly that
   min_complexity is the classification escalation floor while integration
   coverage is independently diff-enforced at all complexities.

7. security / low — No new material authorization or data-exposure surface. But
   this change makes git invocation more central to blocking behavior; if commit
   values originate from CLI input, unsafe command construction would turn
   invalid-input handling into a command-injection risk. Confirm
   git_helpers._run_git accepts an argv list with shell=False and that the HEAD
   fallback uses the same path.

ROUND 1 FINDINGS (openai) — all dispositioned before round 2

1. approach / high — ERROR vs FAIL status mismatch between AC and plan.
2. edge-case / medium — rev-parse --git-dir non-zero conflates broken git with
   non-repo, turning genuine infrastructure faults into a green skip.
3. dependency / medium — _infra_result may have unreviewed callers.
4. edge-case / me […truncated]

findings.finding: test_integration_coverage_reads_the_per_run_entry_after_a_restore became VACUOUS: tmp_path is not a git work tree, so the new git_context probe returns not_git and the gate SKIPs, satisfying 'assert result.ok is True' without exercising the per-run-entry preference it exists to pin. FIXED: stubbed git_context to work_tree and strengthened the assertion to 'ok is True and not is_skipped'. Mutation-verified — removing the per-run entry preference now fails the test, where it passed before the fix.

Stale 'At medium+' in the prose the agent executes when deciding what to put in the ledger — a small run would conclude no integration behavior is needed and then be blocked at F11 with the work already built. FIXED: rewritten to 'At every complexity' with the run-id citation, plus an explicit note that this is the one ledger obligation small does not buy out of.

The primary user-facing small-vs-medium trade-off list still named integration coverage among the checks that report 'skipped' at small. Now false. FIXED: removed from the list and replaced with an explicit callout that integration coverage is the one check small does not get out of.

(a) The docstring still contrasted itself with 'the cross_component gate's medium+ floor', which this change removed — and the iterate spec quotes that sentence as its evidence, so the diff invalidated its own cited authority. (b) integration_coverage claimed 'same posture as check_ci_supplychain_ack' while that gate still uses the binary rev-parse --git-dir probe, so the parity does not hold on the git-probe axis. FIXED (docstrings), DEFERRED (probe migration): the ci_supplychain parenthetical now records that the floors are aligned and carries an explicit NOTE that its git probe is still the binary form, i.e. the fail-open class git_context was extracted to remove; integration_coverage's claim is narrowed to 'same COMPLEXITY posture' with the divergence named. Migrating that third gate's probe is a behaviour change outside this card's scope and is filed as triage rather than smuggled in.

Docstring still described its None return as rendered 'ERROR (medium+) / SKIP'; there is no SKIP path from it any more. FIXED, together with the module docstring. Compressed so the file stays at exactly its base 300 lines rather than growing a file already at the guideline.

The new HEAD fallback called _run_git with no timeout while every other git probe on the path is bounded (10s / 30s). A stalled mount that had already answered the cached metadata probe would hang F11 with no report — the opposite of the fail-closed refusal the change exists to produce. FIXED: timeout=10.0 added, matching git_context; a timeout yields rc != 0 and lands on the existing 'HEAD is unresolvable' ERROR.

A code comment asserted find_entry_by_run_id 'never raises', and the mini-plan recorded that as verified at code. False: lib/iterate_entry.py catches only (JSONDecodeError, OSError), and UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError subclass, so a non-UTF-8 entry file propagates. FIXED (comment), DEFERRED (store fix): the comment now states the real invariant and names the UnicodeDecodeError path as pre-existing and fail-closed. The one-word store fix touches a shared reader used well beyond this gate and is filed as triage rather than made without its own test.

git_context returned a bare str and both callers branched on the two failure names then fell through to PROCEED — putting an unrecognised state on the fail-OPEN path, in a helper whose whole purpose is fail-closed classification. FIXED: return type pinned as Literal['work_tree','not_git','git_error'], the contract documented in the docstring, and BOTH callers inverted to proceed only on an explicit work_tree.

At trivial the gate is unsatisfiable — the Test Completeness Ledger is auto-n/a there, so there are no behaviors to mark — but the remedy text offered only routes that cannot be performed at that tier. FIXED: _floor_note now names escalation to medium as the only executable route at trivial, and its docstring records why.

Two non-git tests sweep four complexities although _git_precheck's not_git arm never reads complexity, so six of the eight cases cannot fail differentially — advertising mutation coverage the sweep does not provide. FIXED: sweep kept but documented as an invariant record rather than a differential guard, contrasted with the two sweeps below where the parameter genuinely is the guard.

_floor_note's defensive normalization (str / strip / lower) was unpinned — every seeded entry is already a clean lowercase literal, so deleting it left the suite green and a legacy ' Small ' entry would silently lose its floor note. FIXED: added a 12-case direct unit test over {}, None, non-string values, ' SMALL ', 'TRIVIAL', medium and large, asserting both that a note appears exactly when substantiable and that it never claims a floor it cannot.

Claim under doubt: the trivial remedy text is correct (Stage-2 finding 11: escalation is the only executable route at trivial) — False at source. check_integration_coverage reads only test_completeness.behaviors — never status, and since the reorder never complexity. check_test_completeness_ledger SKIPs at trivial so nothing validates the block's shape, and append_iterate_entry splats --entry-json extras verbatim. So a trivial run satisfies the gate by recording the behavior. The shipped operator text sent it to mid-flight escalation instead, buying an iterate spec, mini-plan, approval gate, external plan review and full test suite it did not need — the same species of overclaim this card exists to remove, reintroduced inside the fix's own remedy.

Claim under doubt: AC-10 is satisfied — the supersession is recorded — No decision drop for this run exists in either root, while four other 2026-08-01 runs have theirs. The artifact is gitignored, so it is structurally invisible to a diff-reading Stage-1 reviewer — an AC nobody can check by reading the diff.

Claim under doubt: the two deferrals are owned — reviews.json says both are 'filed as triage' — Neither card existed. Zero hits for UnicodeDecodeError, git_context or rev-parse --git-dir across the worktree triage store, the main-root store and the main-root outbox. Both deferrals were recorded ONLY as prose NOTEs inside the code they defer — precisely the 'carrying no owner' state this run's own spec header criticises about the IT-3 anchor. A false statement in a durable record.

Claim under doubt: the gate is non-dodgeable at every complexity — The shared-results fallback read iterate_latest.test_completeness with NO run-id attribution, while its three siblings (check_test_completeness_ledger, check_surface_verification, silent_revert_declarations) all guard the same file with read_iterate_latest(...).is_current. On a branch behind main F11 restores that file to HEAD, so an unattributed read sees the PREVIOUS run's block — and a cross-component change passes green crediting someone else's integration test. This change widened that hole from medium+ to all four tiers while strengthening the docstring's non-dodgeability claim.

Claim under doubt: AC-3 holds: not_git SKIPs at every complexity, preserving the CLI sandbox contract — git_context classified not_git ONLY by English substring match on stderr. In a non-git directory rev-parse exits 128, so the substring was the sole discriminator — and git uses gettext with Git-for-Windows shipping translations. On a localized install (this operator's environment is German) a genuine non-git directory returns a translated fatal, matches neither phrase, and classifies git_error: both gates then ERROR on a non-git project, inverting AC-3, and the CLI sandbox suite goes red on that machine while green here. The external plan review raised this and the disposition answered it by preserving the logic byte-for-byte, which does not address brittleness — and this change then promoted that classifier from 1 gate x 2 tiers to 2 gates x 4 tiers.

Claim under doubt: AC-9 — runtime prose matches the code — The NORMATIVE Phase Matrix became internally contradictory at trivial: 'Test Completeness Ledger | n/a (auto)' sits directly above 'Integration Coverage | if cross_component', and the only artifact that satisfies integration coverage is a Ledger behavior. The table is declared the single source of truth for phase selection, and the agent reads it long before it could see the _floor_note remedy.

Claim under doubt: the vacuous-test class was swept — only test_derived_snapshots.py:236 was affected — A second survivor: test_layer_coverage_core.py::test_gates_skip_cleanly_below_medium asserts both gates SKIP on a bare tmp_path. It passes only because tmp_path is non-git and is completely blind to this change's core mutation — restore _is_enforcing inside _infra_result and it still passes. Its NAME and comment now assert a property the diff deleted for removal_coverage, so a reader grepping 'below medium' finds a green test claiming the opposite of the code.

Claim under doubt: the user-facing guide now matches the new behaviour — guide.md documented the integration-coverage half but was silent on the half most likely to surprise: removal_coverage infra failures now BLOCK at trivial and small. Separately 'Integration coverage is the one you do not get out of' was imprecise — removal coverage and check_ci_supplychain_ack also never stand down by level.

Claim under doubt: the new tests prove 'at every complexity' rather than sampling it — test_check_integration_coverage_infra.py's git_error sweep seeds no entry and returns before find_entry_by_run_id is reached, so all four parameterized cases are byte-identical and cannot fail differentially — advertising coverage it does not provide.

Claim under doubt: the newly-reachable git_error block is diagnosable — git_context discards stderr, and both callers printed a guessed cause list that omitted the two most likely real causes (safe.directory / dubious ownership, and a localized fatal). For a change whose thesis is 'a gate that cannot run must FAIL', the failure could not name why.

Claim under doubt: (reviewer's own hypothesis, SELF-REFUTED) the None-diff ERROR opens a new false-red class via the ensure_current merge commit — Refuted by the reviewer during construction: check_ci_supplychain_ack already runs at every complexity, uses the same _iterate_changed_paths, and already ERRORs on None — so that scenario already produces a red F11 today. This change adds a second identical block, not a new blocked class.

catch UnicodeDecodeError/ValueError around find_entry_by_run_id and treat the entry as unavailable; make _floor_note accept object | None and return no note unless isinstance(entry, dict).  ACCEPTED AND FIXED. This was a real gap between my own acceptance criterion and the code: AC-11 promises a malformed entry is absent rather than fatal, and I had deferred the store fix to triage while leaving the AC unqualified. Absorbed at THIS gate's call site via a new _read_entry helper (catching ValueError/OSError, which covers UnicodeDecodeError and JSONDecodeError) rather than by loosening a shared reader other callers depend on; the store fix stays tracked as trg-06216b9f. _floor_note now takes object | None and isinstance-guards. Fail-closed direction preserved: an unreadable entry means no self-report, and a cross-component diff still ERRORs.  2. test / medium — test_check_integration_coverage.py:162. The malformed-entry test covers invalid JSON only (whose store-reader path is intentionally skipped) and not the non-UTF-8 path or the non-dict entry AC-11 names, leaving a specified failure mode unvalidated.  ACCEPTED AND FIXED. Added test_non_utf8_entry_file_fails_closed_instead_of_raising (writes structurally valid JSON with a lone 0xff continuation byte) and test_a_non_dict_entry_is_treated_as_absent. Mutation-verified: removing the absorption makes the first fail with the exact UnicodeDecodeError the reviewer predicted.  3. spec / low — AC-10 requires an ADR decision drop via write_decision_drop.py keyed by the run id, superseding MUST-FIX 1 and SHOULD-FIX 6; the diff updates prose and comments but contains no drop artifact.  ACCEPTED — ordering, not omission. F3 runs during finalization, after this review step (Step 8 precedes F6 by design, so a review that runs later reviews shipped code). The drop is written at F3 naming both superseded decisions with the ci_supplychain contradiction as evidence. Also raised independently by the Stage-3 doubt reviewer, who accepted the same basis.  Overall assessment (reviewer): "The core enforcement reorder, tri-state git handling, and removal-gate ordering are substantially implemented and well tested, but the explicit malformed-entry fail-closed contract and required supersession record need fixes before shipping."

external_code.raw_excerpt:
External CODE review (mode=code, provider=openrouter). Subject: the code + prose
diff vs merge-base 6d2b2013 (shared/, plugins/, docs/ — 108,128 chars). The
planning artifacts were passed as --spec-file rather than diffed, so this is a
review of the change, not a narrowed subset chosen to beat truncation.

Reviewers: openai = success (verdict: revise); gemini = degraded (provider
returned an empty reply) — recorded degraded, NOT counted as an approval.

FINDINGS

1. bug / medium — integration_coverage.py:194. A malformed iterate entry can still
   RAISE instead of producing the required blocking result. find_entry_by_run_id is
   called without handling UnicodeDecodeError, which the adjacent comment itself
   acknowledges the store does not catch. A non-UTF-8 entry file therefore aborts
   the verifier rather than satisfying AC-11's requirement that malformed entries
   "not raise" and still fail a cross-component diff. Additionally _floor_note
   assumes entry has .get(), so a non-dict value raises AttributeError.
   Suggestion: catch UnicodeDecodeError/ValueError around find_entry_by_run_id and
   treat the entry as unavailable; make _floor_note accept object | None and return
   no note unless isinstance(entry, dict).

   ACCEPTED AND FIXED. This was a real gap between my own acceptance criterion and
   the code: AC-11 promises a malformed entry is absent rather than fatal, and I had
   deferred the store fix to triage while leaving the AC unqualified. Absorbed at
   THIS gate's call site via a new _read_entry helper (catching ValueError/OSError,
   which covers UnicodeDecodeError and JSONDecodeError) rather than by loosening a
   shared reader other callers depend on; the store fix stays tracked as
   trg-06216b9f. _floor_note now takes object | None and isinstance-guards.
   Fail-closed direction preserved: an unreadable entry means no self-report, and a
   cross-component diff still ERRORs.

2. test / medium — test_check_integration_coverage.py:162. The malformed-entry test
   covers invalid JSON only (whose store-reader path is intentionally skipped) and
   not the non-UTF-8 path or the non-dict entry AC-11 names, leaving a specified
   failure mode unvalidated.

   ACCEPTED AND FIXED. Added test_non_utf8_entry_file_fails_closed_instead_of_raising
   (writes structurally valid JSON with a lone 0xff continuation byte) and
   test_a_non_dict_entry_is_treated_as_absent. Mutation-verified: removing the
   absorption makes the first fail with the exact UnicodeDecodeError the reviewer
   predicted.

3. spec / low — AC-10 requires an ADR decision drop via write_decision_drop.py keyed
   by the run id, superseding MUST-FIX 1 and SHOULD-FIX 6; the diff updates prose and
   comments but contains no drop artifact.

   ACCEPTED — ordering, not omission. F3 runs during finalization, after this review
   step (Step 8 precedes F6 by design, so a review that runs later reviews shipped
   code). The drop is written at F3 naming both superseded decisions with the
   ci_supplychain contradiction as evidence. Also raised independently by the
   Stage-3 doubt reviewer, who accepted the same basis.

Overall assessment (reviewer): "The core enforcement reorder, tri-state git
handling, and removal-gate ordering are substantially implemented and well tested,
but the explicit malformed-entry fail-closed contract and required supersession
record need fixes before shipping."
